clips.title: Claude Agent Skills Explained
clips.why: Anthropic's own one-minute picture of what a skill is and how Claude decides to use it.
look: A skill is an organised folder, not a single prompt: instructions plus any files it needs.
Claude picks a skill by itself when it is relevant to the task, which is the job of the description.
clips.after: Our rhino-core skills work the same way: one folder per task, and a description that tells Claude when the task has come up.

clips.title: Don't Build Agents, Build Skills Instead – Barry Zhang & Mahesh Murag, Anthropic
clips.why: The people who built skills at Anthropic define them and explain progressive disclosure, the idea this lesson rests on.
look: How they define a skill: packaged know-how that an agent loads when it needs it.
Progressive disclosure: what the model sees at the start, and what it reads only later.
Think about why this lets one agent carry many skills without slowing down every task.
clips.after: Nova carries every rhino-core skill on every ticket, but pays for a body only when a step needs it, such as plan-and-grill at the planning step.

clips.title: Claude Code Skills from First Principles
clips.why: A walk through the frontmatter fields most people never use, which control who can start a skill and how it runs.
look: Which fields change when a skill is loaded, and who may start it (Claude, a person, or both).
How the description and the other fields work together as the skill's controls.
clips.after: Our skills keep the frontmatter small: a name, a description, a when_to_use line and sometimes an argument hint. Plugin CI checks the rest.

clips.title: Claude Code Plugins Explained In 7 Minutes
clips.why: A short tour of what a plugin is, how its folder is laid out, and how a person installs one.
look: The plugin's folder structure: one manifest, and skills and other parts beside it.
How a person installs a plugin on their machine.
clips.after: Our marketplace, rhino, is the place every engineer and every agent VM installs the same plugins from.

practice.q: Someone types "Lior starts on the frontend team tomorrow, can you write something for the channel?" Which description makes Claude open the welcome skill?

options.why: It says nothing about people joining or welcome messages, so there is nothing to match.

options.text: description: "Writes a two-line welcome for a new teammate: hello by first name, the team, and one tip for day one."
options.why: It names what it produces and the situation (a new teammate), which is what the request is about.

options.text: description: "Use for any message to the team."
options.why: It would match this request, but also every other team message, so it would load where it does not help.

practice.q: The skill welcome-note lives in the plugin team-notes. What does a person type to start it by hand?
practice.hint: Plugin skills get a prefix: the plugin name, a colon, then the skill name.
practice.why: Plugin skills are namespaced, so two plugins can each have a welcome-note without a clash.

practice.q: You changed a skill in a plugin whose plugin.json says "version": "0.1.0". Finish the line so teammates get the change.
practice.hint: Any higher version works; the point is that the string changes.
practice.why: A set version keeps everyone on it until it changes, so a change without a bump reaches nobody.

practice.q: Put what happens in order, from session start to Claude following the skill.
items: The session starts and Claude gets a list of every skill's name and description
A person asks for something that matches one description
Claude calls its Skill tool for that skill
The body of SKILL.md enters the conversation
Claude reads a references/ file only if the body says this task needs it
practice.why: Each layer loads only when the one before it says so: label, then body, then deeper files.

practice.q: Where does SKILL.md go inside a plugin?

options.why: Only plugin.json goes inside .claude-plugin/. Skills there are not found.

options.text: skills/welcome-note/SKILL.md, at the plugin's top level
options.why: Skills, agents, hooks and MCP config all sit at the top level of the plugin; only the manifest is inside .claude-plugin/.

options.text: Anywhere, as long as plugin.json lists the file
options.why: The default place is skills/<name>/SKILL.md. The manifest can add extra folders, but putting it in the standard place needs no listing at all.
